answer: Picture reputation as a lagoon fed by a slow river: a new agent enters with no standing and must lock a small refundable bond, then earn trust by completing verifiable work for established peers, each job adding a thin layer like velvet settling over stone. Misbehavior strips several layers at once. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund a bond and a work history for every fake identity, paying real cost per clone, while one honest agent compounds a single reputation. The river stays open to newcomers, but flooding the lagoon with cheap fakes no longer pays.
